Rashi on Zevachim 13a:10:1.hebrew: והקריבו - דכתיב בעולה, ושחט את בן הבקר, והקריבו בני אהרן את הדם — זו קבלת הדם, וללמד שצריך לקבלו בכלי:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:10:1.english: “And they shall bring near” - For it is written regarding the burnt offering: “And he shall slaughter the young bull… and the sons of Aaron shall bring near the blood” (Leviticus 1:5). This is the collection of the blood, and it teaches that one must collect it in a vessel:

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:11:1.hebrew: אתה אומר כו' או אינו אלא לזריקה - דהא לשון הקרבה למזבח הוא, כדכתיב (ויקרא ז, ט) לכהן המקריב אותה וגו'. והאי נמי בהקרבה למזבח משתעי, דהיינו זריקה. אבל קבלה לא צריך כהן ו[כלי] מאהל מועד ואילך:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:11:1.english: “Do you say…, or is it only referring to sprinkling” - For “presenting” is an expression of bringing [something] to the altar, as it is written (Leviticus 7:9): “the priest who presents it,” etc. And this [verse, too, “shall present,”] speaks of bringing [the blood] to the altar, which is sprinkling. But collection [of the blood] does not require [a priest and] a [service] vessel from the Tent of Meeting onward.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:11:2.hebrew: כשהוא אומר כו' זו קבלת הדם - כדאשכחן קבלה בעולת סיני (שמות כ״ד:ו׳): ויקח משה חצי הדם וישם באגנות. ואע"ג דהקרבה לשון הולכה היא, כדאמרן לעיל (זבחים דף ד.): והקריב הכהן את הכל — זו הולכת אברים לכבש — הכא, כיון דזימנין הולכה ליתיה כלל, כמו השוחט בצד המזבח, לא כתב לה קרא, ואקבלה הוא דאכתביה. והיכא דאיצטריכא הולכה, נפקא לן דהויא עבודה מדאפקא רחמנא לקבלה בלשון הולכה:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:11:2.english: When it says, etc. “this is collection of the blood” - As we find collection [of blood] in the burnt offering at Sinai (Exodus 24:6): “And Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins.” And although “presenting” (hakravah) is a term of carrying (holacha), as we said above (Zevachim 4a): “And the priest shall present all” — this is the carrying of the limbs to the ramp — here, since there are times when there is no carrying at all, such as one who slaughters beside the altar, Scripture would not have written it [here] with reference to carrying; rather, it wrote it with reference to collection. And where carrying is needed, we derive that it is a [valid] service from the fact that the Merciful One expressed collection in the language of carrying.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:11:3.hebrew: בכהן כשר - לאפוקי חללים ובעלי מומין:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:11:3.english: By a fit priest - To exclude *chalalim* (priests of flawed lineage) and those with blemishes.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:11:4.hebrew: ובכלי שרת - שיהו מלובשים בגדי כהונה, דכהנים משמע (הכהנים) בכיהונם (לקמן זבחים דף יח:), והיינו בגדי כהונה. וכל היכא דקתני נמי "בכהן כשר ובכלי שרת" — בבגדי כהונה קאמר:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:11:4.english: And with service vessels - That they must be wearing priestly garments, as "the priests" implies [priests] in their priesthood (below, Zevachim 18b), and that is the priestly garments. And wherever it teaches as well "by a fit priest and with service vessels," it is speaking of priestly garments.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:12:1.hebrew: אמר רבי עקיבא - ר' עקיבא לא משמע ליה מהכא, דאיכא למימר בני אהרן כל שהן, והכהנים בכיהונם לא משמע ליה:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:12:1.english: Rabbi Akiva said - Rabbi Akiva does not understand [the law] from here, since one could say that "the sons of Aaron" [means] any of them at all, and he does not understand "the priests" [to mean] in their priesthood.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:12:2.hebrew: מה להלן בכהנים כשרין - הכתוב מדבר, דהא אלעזר ואיתמר כתיבי. ובכלי שרת נמי הכתוב מדבר, דכתיב שם אשר מלא את ידם, והיינו לשון רבוי בגדי כהונה, דכתיב (ויקרא כא) ומלא את ידו ללבוש את הבגדים, וכתיב נמי ובגדי הקדש אשר לאהרן יהיו לבניו אחריו למשחה בהם למלא בם את ידם (שמות כט):
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:12:2.english: Just as there, [it refers] to fit priests - The verse is speaking [of them], for Elazar and Itamar are written [there]. And [it is] also [speaking] of service vestments, for it is written [there], “whom he consecrated [lit., filled their hand]”, and this is an expression of increase, [referring to] the priestly garments, as it is written (Leviticus 21), “and who is consecrated [lit., filled his hand] to put on the garments,” and it is also written, “And the holy garments of Aaron shall be for his sons after him, to be anointed in them and to consecrate them [lit., to fill their hand in them]” (Exodus 29):

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:13:1.english: To discern a difference, etc. - And yet you treat the collection like the other services:

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:13:2.hebrew: ואין לי לפרש - איני יודע לפרש מה הפרש שמעתי ביניהן:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:13:2.english: And I cannot explicate - I do not know how to explain what distinction I heard between them.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:14:1.hebrew: לא עשה בה מחשבה כמעשה - השתא סלקא דעתך הא דקאמר אין מחשבה פוסלת בשבילה, אם חישב בה חוץ לזמנו או שלא לשמו, אלמא לא פסלה בקבלה:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:14:1.english: He did not render intent like action - Now it enters your mind [to understand] that which [the Tanna] said, "intent does not disqualify on its account," [to mean that] if one had intent during it [i.e., the collection] to offer outside its time or not for its own sake, evidently [the Torah] did not disqualify through collection.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:14:2.hebrew: קבלו בחוץ אינו חייב כרת - דשחיטה היא, והפסוק דכתיב לחיובא כרת בחוץ [ואל פתח אהל מועד] נאמר בשחיטה, וזריקה נפקא מדם יחשב, לקמן בפרק השוחט (זבחים דף קז.):
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:14:2.english: If he collected it outside, he is not liable to karet - Because [collection] is [in the category of] slaughter, and [the verse] that is written to impose liability — [karet for an offering outside] — "And [he did not bring it] to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting" — is [stated] regarding slaughter; but [liability for] sprinkling is derived from "blood shall be reckoned" (Leviticus 17:4), below in the chapter HaShochet (Zevachim 107a).

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:14:3.hebrew: קבלו פסולין - זרים ושאר חייבי מיתות, כגון שתויי יין והדומין להם:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:14:3.english: [If] unfit [persons] collected it - [Meaning,] non-priests and others liable to death [for performing the service], such as those who are intoxicated with wine and the like.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:15:1.hebrew: אתה דורש - מאיליך, ומסכים למה ששמעתי:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:15:1.english: You expound - on your own, and you concur with what I heard.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:16:1.hebrew: מחשבת פיגול - שהיא מחשבת דחוץ לזמנו, לא פסלה בקבלה:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:16:1.english: Intent of piggul - [Meaning, the intent] to [offer or consume] beyond its time; this does not disqualify [the offering] at the stage of receiving [the blood].

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:17:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי - דיוק זה נכון שהרי [דתנא] דמתניתין לא איירי במחשבת פיגול:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:17:1.english: This is also precise - [For] the Tanna of the mishna is not speaking of an intention of piggul.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:18:1.hebrew: מחשבת פיגול - מחשבה דחוץ לזמנו לא פסלה בקבלה:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:18:1.english: Intent of piggul - [Intent] to eat outside its [proper] time does not disqualify [the offering] during the collection [of the blood].

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:18:2.hebrew: ושפיכת שירים לא פסלה בהו מחשבה - דקתני לעיל: יכול שאני מרבה אף שפיכת שיריים:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:18:2.english: And [improper] intent does not disqualify the pouring of the remainder [of the blood] - As it taught above: "I might think that I include even the pouring of the remainder [of the blood]."

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:19:1.hebrew: אלא בזריקה - במחשב בשעת זריקה ע"מ לאכול מזבחו ביום השלישי, כדכתיב בקרא דמחשבת פיגול "המקריב אותו לא יחשב", ילפינן מיניה בפ"ב (לקמן זבחים כט.): במחשב בשעת הקרבה לאכול מזבחו ביום השלישי הכתוב מדבר, [והקרבה] היינו זריקה:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:19:1.english: Only with sprinkling - [That is, only] when one has the intent, at the time of sprinkling, to eat from his sacrifice on the third day, as it is written in the verse about the intent of piggul: "He who offers it shall not be credited." We derive from it in the second chapter (below, Zevachim 29a): The verse speaks of one who has intent at the time of offering to eat from his sacrifice on the third day; and [the word] "offering" means sprinkling.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:19:2.hebrew: בדברים המביאים - את הקרבן לידי היתר אכילה, הכתוב מדבר:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:19:2.english: With matters that bring - the offering to the permissibility of eating, the verse speaks.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:1:1.hebrew: צד כרת לא פריך - לפי שאינו שוה בשניהם: דחטאת אינו ענוש כרת על הבאתו, אלא שעל שגגת כרת הוא בא, ופסח ענוש כרת על הבאתו:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:1:1.english: The element of karet does not refute - Because it is not the same in both: for a sin offering, one is not liable to karet for [failing to] bring it; rather, it comes [to atone] for the inadvertent [transgression of a prohibition punishable by] karet. But a Paschal offering — one is liable to karet for [failing to] bring it.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:20:1.hebrew: אף שפיכת שירים - אם שפך שירי הדם ליסוד על מנת לאכול בשר חוץ לזמנו, או אם הקטיר אימורין במחשבה זו:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:20:1.english: Even the pouring of the remainder - If one poured the remainder of the blood on the base [of the altar] with the intention of eating the flesh outside its [proper] time, or if one burned the sacrificial portions with this thought:

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:21:1.hebrew: לא ירצה - היינו זריקה, שהיא מרצה:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:21:1.english: It shall not be accepted - This refers to the sprinkling of the blood, which brings acceptance.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:21:2.hebrew: בכלל היתה - זריקה בכלל הדברים המביאין לידי אכילה:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:21:2.english: Was included - Sprinkling was included in the category of the things that bring about eating.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:21:3.hebrew: שאין מעכבין - שירים אין מעכבין, כדתניא באיזהו מקומן (לקמן זבחים דף נב.): יכול יעכבנו? תלמוד לומר "ואת כל הדם ישפך" — נתקו הכתוב ועשאו שירי מצוה כו'. הקטרת אימורין לא מעכבין כפרה, דכתיב "הדם הוא בנפש יכפר":
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:21:3.english: That do not prevent - The remainders do not prevent [atonement], as it was taught in the baraita [in the chapter] "Eizehu Mekoman" (later, Zevachim 52a): One might think that [not pouring them] prevents it. The verse states, "And all the blood he shall pour out" — the verse separated it and made it a remainder of the commandment, etc. The burning of the sacrificial portions does not prevent atonement, as it is written, "For it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul."

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:2:1.hebrew: אשם נמי לייתי - לפסול בשלא לשמו מבנין אב, כדאמר רבי אליעזר לעיל (זבחים דף י:), דקא"ל רבי יהושע חוזרני חלילה. ופרכינן: וליהדר דינא ולייתי במה הצד! וסליקנא להך אתקפתא משום דאיכא למיפרך: מה להצד השוה שבהן, שכן יש בהן צד כרת. ומשני: לבן עזאי אשם מפירכא אחריתא מסלק ליה, דלא לייתי בבנין אב, דפריך: מה להצד השוה שבהן שישנו בצבור! פסח קרי ליה קרבן צבור, כדאמרן בסדר יומא בפ' הוציאו לו (יומא דף נא.), משום דאתי בכינופיא:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:2:1.english: Let a guilt offering too be derived - to disqualify it when offered not for its own sake, from a binyan av, as Rabbi Eliezer said above (Zevachim 10b), when Rabbi Yehoshua said to him, "I go around in a circle" [i.e., the argument cycles back]. And we challenge: But let the argument return, and let it be derived through "what is the common aspect"! And I resolve that objection because it can be refuted: What of the common aspect among them, for they have an aspect of karet! And [the Gemara] answers: According to Ben Azzai, the guilt offering is removed by a different refutation, so that it is not derived through a binyan av, as it refutes: What of the common aspect among them, that it exists as a communal offering! The Pesach it calls a communal offering, as we said in the order of Yoma in the chapter "Hotzi'u Lo" (Yoma 51a), because it comes in an assembly.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:4:1.hebrew: גמרא גמיר לה - מפי ע"ב זקנים, כדתנן:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:4:1.english: He learned it as a tradition - From the seventy-two Elders, as we learned in a mishnah:

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:4:2.hebrew: לחדד תלמידיו - שיקשו לו תשובה עליו. או א"נ אחרת: שיתנו לבם להיות חריפין, לדרוש קלים וחמורים מאיליהן, כבן עזאי:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:4:2.english: To sharpen his students - So that they would raise a refutation against it. Alternatively, that they would set their minds to be sharp, to derive kalim va'chamurim (a fortiori inferences) on their own, like ben Azzai.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:5:1.hebrew: וקבל והלך וזרק כו' - "או" "או" קתני: קבל, או הלך, או זרק:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:5:1.english: And he collected, conveyed, and sprinkled, etc. - It teaches "or… or…": [that is,] he collected, or he conveyed, or he sprinkled.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:5:2.hebrew: או לשמו ושלא לשמו - שחישב בעבודה אחת לשמו ושלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:5:2.english: Or for its sake and not for its sake - That he had in mind, during a single service, [both] for its sake and not for its sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:8:1.hebrew: אבל אפשר בלא הילוך - הלכך לא חשיבא למיפסל:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:8:1.english: But it is possible without conveying - Therefore, it is not significant enough to disqualify [the offering].

Rashi on Zevachim 13a:9:1.hebrew: המהלך במקום שהוא צריך להוליך - הולכה זו מחשבה פוסלת בה, אם חישב בה שלא לשמה. ובגמ' מפרש למילתי', מאי צריך ומאי אין צריך:
Rashi on Zevachim 13a:9:1.english: One who conveys in a place where he is required to convey - Concerning this conveying, intent disqualifies it, if he had intent during it for the sake of something other than the offering's proper designation. And in the Gemara, [Rabbi Eliezer] explains his statement: what is "required" and what is "not required."

Tosafot on Zevachim 13a:11:1.hebrew: אתה אומר זו קבלת הדם כו' - לעיל (זבחים דף ד.), פי' בקונט', דמוקמינן והקריבו בקבלה ולא בהולכה, משום דוהקריבו נאמר מיד אחר שחיטה, וקבלה היא עבודה ראשונה שאחר שחיטה. ולפירושו קשה, היכי בעי למימר הכא "או אינו אלא זריקה"? אלא נראה דמוקמי' לה בקבלה או בזריקה, לפי שהן עבודות חשובות שאי אפשר לבטלן, מה שאין כן בהולכה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 13a:11:1.english: “You say: this is collection of the blood,” etc. - Above (Zevachim 4a), Rashi explained in his commentary that we establish “and they shall present” as referring to collection and not to conveying [the blood], because “and they shall present” is stated immediately after the slaughter, and collection is the first service after the slaughter. But according to his explanation, it is difficult: how could [the Gemara] say here, “or is it only sprinkling”? Rather, it appears that we establish it as referring to collection or to sprinkling, because these are significant services that cannot be omitted, unlike conveying [the blood].

Tosafot on Zevachim 13a:11:2.hebrew: בכהן כשר ובכלי שרת - פירש בקונטרס: כלי שרת — בגדי כהונה. וקשה, דהא נפקא לקמן בפרק שני (זבחים דף יז:) מקרא דאין בגדיהם עליהן, אין כהונה עליהן, והוו להו זרים, ואפילו בעבודה דלא מעכבא כפרה. ויש לומר, דאי לאו גזרה שוה דהכא, הוה אמרינן: מה שהקפידה תורה אמחוסר בגדים, היינו היכא דכתיבי בגדים, אבל היכא דלא כתיבי בגדים — לא. וגבי נתינת אש וסידור איברים לא הוה בעינא בגדים מכהן בכיהונו. אלא מדגלי רחמנא גבי קבלה גזרה שוה, ילפינן בכל דוכתא דהכהן הוי בכיהונו:
Tosafot on Zevachim 13a:11:2.english: "By a fit priest and in service vestments" - Rashi explained in the commentary: "Service vestments" means the priestly garments. But this is difficult, for this is derived later, in the second chapter (Zevachim 17b), from the verse "when their garments are upon them, their priesthood is upon them" — [meaning] if their garments are not upon them, their priesthood is not upon them, and they are considered non-priests (zarim), even in a service that does not affect atonement. And one can answer: Were it not for the verbal analogy (gezerah shavah) here, we would have said: That which the Torah was particular about regarding [a priest] lacking garments applies only where garments are written [explicitly]; but where garments are not written, [it does] not. And with regard to placing the fire and arranging the limbs, I would not have required garments, [i.e., that the service be done by] a priest in his priestly status. But since the Merciful One revealed the verbal analogy regarding collection [of the blood], we derive in every place that the priest must be in his priestly status:

Tosafot on Zevachim 13a:17:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי דקתני שהזבח נפסל - במסקנא לא חיישינן להאי דיקא, דבקבלה נמי איכא פסול פיגול. ויש לפרש: במסקנא דנקט לשון פסול, דאיירי בשלא לשמן, דהוי בכל ד' עבודות. ומיהו אשכחן דיקא דלא קאי לבסוף, גבי "כל הנישום דמים באחר" (קדושין דף כח:):
Tosafot on Zevachim 13a:17:1.english: The language is also precise, as it teaches that the offering is disqualified - In the conclusion [of the Gemara] we are not concerned with this inference, since with receiving the blood too there is a disqualification of piggul. And one can explain that in the conclusion, [the mishna] used the term "disqualified" because it is dealing with [intent to offer it] not for their own sake, which applies to all four service acts. However, we do find an inference that does not stand in the end, regarding "anything that is appraised by money for another" (Kiddushin 28b).
